one_liner: Neo4j has the Aura management REST API (OAuth2 client credentials) plus per-database HTTP Query API (Basic/Bearer) and an official MCP server; there is no single multi-tenant SaaS API, and the database APIs are per-instance.
auth_notes: Aura API uses OAuth 2.0 client credentials (client ID/secret exchanged at /oauth/token for a Bearer token). The database HTTP/Query API accepts Basic (username:password) and Bearer tokens. The Aura OAuth flow is not an authorization-code flow for third-party apps, so each user supplies their own client credentials. Treating that as API_KEY-like is a judgement call.
access_notes: AuraDB Free needs no credit card and gives instance credentials, which cover the Query API and Bolt. Aura API credentials are available to all tiers per the current docs. The older classic docs said Free and Professional users needed billing info first, so there is some conflict.
blocker_notes: Per-customer setup is needed: each user must supply their own instance URL and credentials, or Aura client credentials. There is no central multi-tenant OAuth app. Docs and the Aura API's free-tier credential requirements are somewhat inconsistent.

evidence.quote: The Aura API uses OAuth 2.0 for API authentication.
Request are authorized through an `Authorization` header. Both *basic* and *bearer* authentication are supported.
All tiers can create Aura API credentials. API credentials are linked to the user account, inheriting its capabilities and roles.
No credit card or other payment method required
Use the same principles to authorize requests to the HTTP Query API instead, as described in [Query API → Authorize requests]
If you are looking for the official product Neo4j MCP server please find it [here](https://github.com/neo4j/mcp).
